## Three countries and five main parts of the journey

Rio introduces you to Sugar Loaf, Corcovado and the oceanfront neighbourhoods. At Iguazu, you see the waterfalls from both the Brazilian and Argentine sides. Buenos Aires brings tango, historic districts and the option of a visit to a gaucho ranch. In Chile, the journey begins in Santiago and on the coast at Valparaíso, then heads north to San Pedro de Atacama for Moon Valley, high-altitude lagoons, the salt flat and the El Tatio geysers.

## What makes this route distinctive

### Rio de Janeiro: between the ocean and the mountains

The first 3 days centre on Rio's 2 main viewpoints. Sugar Loaf opens up the coastline, while Corcovado reveals another side of the city through the Tijuca Forest. The views take in Copacabana, Ipanema, Leme, Guanabara Bay, the Rio–Niterói Bridge, the Botanical Garden and Maracanã Stadium.

The visit to Sugar Loaf begins at Praia Vermelha and continues via Urca Hill. The first viewing platform has restaurants and bars, before the cable car climbs higher. After the descent, the tour continues through the historic districts. The Corcovado excursion starts at the railway station, where a train climbs through the jungle to the summit and the statue of Christ the Redeemer.

These 2 perspectives reveal both Rio's natural setting and its historic architecture. Between excursions, there is time for the beaches and the ocean.

### Iguazu: the Brazilian and Argentine sides

The falls are visited from both countries. The Brazilian side offers broad views of the 275 cascades. On the Argentine side, walkways run above and alongside the falling water. The Devil's Throat is a focal point on both sides.

On the Brazilian side, you can add the Macuco Safari: a jeep ride through the jungle, a walk to the river and a boat trip close to the falls. It costs USD 135 per person. Another optional visit is the Bird Park, at USD 60 per person.

The Argentine national park covers 55,500 hectares. Paths and viewing platforms bring you close to individual cascades before you reach the main waterfall.

### Buenos Aires: architecture, tango and gauchos

In Buenos Aires, the focus shifts from nature to the city. The sightseeing tour includes La Boca, San Telmo, Plaza Dorrego, Plaza de Mayo, Casa Rosada, Recoleta and modern districts. A key landmark is the 67 m Obelisk on Avenida 9 de Julio.

In the evening, enjoy a tango show with dinner and Argentine wines. Tango developed in the port neighbourhoods among immigrants and working people.

The following day is free, with optional excursions available. One option is Fiesta Gaucha at a ranch about 80 km from Buenos Aires. This roughly 8-hour trip includes a traditional lunch and demonstrations of gaucho horsemanship and skills with lassos and boleadoras.

### Santiago and the Chilean coast

The Santiago tour begins in the historic centre. La Moneda was built in the final years of Spanish rule as the royal mint and later became the seat of government. Around Plaza de Armas are the Cathedral, City Hall, Central Post Office and other historic buildings.

Santa Lucía Hill offers a panorama of the capital. The route then continues through the modern districts of Vitacura, Las Condes and Providencia.

The next day, travel towards the Pacific through the Curacaví and Casablanca valleys. Casablanca is known for white wines, including Sauvignon Blanc. Valparaíso spreads across hills connected by historic funiculars. Visits include Plaza Victoria, Plaza Sotomayor and Paseo 21 de Mayo. Continue to Viña del Mar for its parks, beaches and Quinta Vergara.

### Atacama: a contrasting finale

The final part of the journey takes you to northern Chile. After flying to Calama, transfer to San Pedro de Atacama. Moon Valley reveals the dry landscapes of the Cordillera de la Sal and Los Flamencos National Reserve. Sunset brings gold and red tones to the desert, with Andean volcanoes on the horizon.

The next day includes the Miscanti and Miñiques lagoons, Socaire, the Salar de Atacama salt flat, Chaxa Lagoon and Toconao. The flamingo reserve is home to 3 species. In Toconao, visit San Lucas Church and its bell tower.

The last excursion begins before dawn. El Tatio lies above 4,000 m, and the fumaroles are most active early in the morning. On the return journey, look out for vicuñas and viscachas and stop in Machuca.

## Getting from place to place

The route involves flights from Rio to Iguazu, Iguazu to Buenos Aires, Buenos Aires to Santiago, Santiago to Calama and Calama to Santiago. The Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires–Santiago flights are included in the Word 2027 programme. The Santiago–Calama–Santiago flights are listed separately as not included, subject to confirmation.

The main sightseeing programme uses group excursions with English-speaking guides, and group transfers with drivers.

## Practical details

Accommodation is in 4-star hotels or equivalent properties, with breakfast. Food and drinks during transfers are extra unless specifically included.

International flights are not included.

This is a busy journey: 3 nights in Rio, 2 at Iguazu, 3 in Buenos Aires, 4 in Santiago across two stays and 2 in San Pedro de Atacama. The Atacama section includes an early departure to geysers above 4,000 m, where morning temperatures may fall below −2 °C.
